question: What segmentation and repetition can be established on original images before assigning Latin readings or a modern-language meaning?
selected_object: MMA1988.433.2 / Met327384, linked CDLI number P005390 requires later verification
selection_reason: A new photographed early tablet with public institutional images and reported multiple views; selected for image access, not a match to a Kazakh word.
prior_exposure: Museum/search title and general attribution to grain account already seen; no individual transliteration read. Thus graph-first, not semantically blind. Model prior knowledge cannot be erased.
no_circularity: Do not use ama/adda as raw facts: distinguish physical impression, tentative graph, sign-list identification, proposed sound, proposed meaning, and historical etymology.
Assign neutral IDs to tentative repeated complexes and record pixel boxes; uncertain sign boundaries remain uncertain.
No synthetic completion, rotation or contrast change unless recorded. Native crops allowed.
Do not infer a sound from resemblance to a Kazakh word; external phonetic constraints must be explicitly identified as evidence or hypotheses.
quality_gate: At least six individually distinguishable impressions or complexes, distinct strokes on native image, and visible cell boundaries; otherwise unresolved.
sampling: First front image in official Met API; then first distinct additional image in API order. Save all available image URLs and metadata, do not select by matching content.
prediction: An account-like graphic model predicts recurring nonnumerically-assigned graphic complexes with variable impression bundles in segregated cells. Competing explanations include labels, personal names, fixed headings, seal impressions and decorative marks.
freeze: Record native observations and hashes before opening this object individual editorial rows.
separate_target_audit: Existing P232300 photo may be audited as source for the previously discussed ama/adda candidates. Its readings are already known; no blind claim and no transfer of its catalogue labels to unreadable wedges.
scope: One new object at most two official views plus a clearly separated audit of an existing image; no independent full phonetic decipherment promised.
